output.preview:
Persistence

LangGraph has a built-in persistence layer, implemented through checkpointers. When you compile a graph with a checkpointer, it saves a checkpoint of the graph state at every super-step. Checkpoints are saved to a thread, which can be accessed after graph execution. Because threads keep the state after execution, this enables human-in-the-loop, memory, time travel and fault tolerance.

Threads

A thread is a unique ID assigned to each checkpoint saved by a checkpointer…

- For us: record every model call and tool result as a step. On restart, replay recorded results instead of calling the model again (saves money and keeps the run consistent).

output.preview:
Idempotent requests

The API supports idempotency for safely retrying requests without accidentally performing the same operation twice. When creating or updating an object, use an idempotency key. Then, if a connection error occurs, you can safely repeat the request without risk of creating a second object or performing the update twice.

To perform an idempotent request, provide an additional Idempotency-Key header to the request.

Stripe's idempotency works by saving the resulting status code and body of the first request made for any given idempotency key, regardless of whether it succeeds or fails…

- For agents: derive the key from (run id, tool-call id), so a replayed or retried step re-sends the same key and the side effect happens once.

A Retry Policy is a collection of settings that tells Temporal how and when to try again after something fails in a Workflow Execution or Activity Task Execution.

Default behavior

Activities are retried by default with exponential backoff (initial interval 1 second, backoff coefficient 2.0, maximum interval 100 times the initial interval) and no limit on attempts. Workflow Executions are not retried by default.
